correctness.rationale: The degree-one real slice of the published cone is an intersection of local tripod tetrahedra. All coordinate values lie in [0,1]. A connected fractional support with a tree component has at least two leaf endpoints and more edges than internal vertices; a cycle-with-tail fractional component has at least one leaf endpoint and likewise has more edges than internal vertices. At most one independent tight equation is contributed per internal vertex, so any such point is nonextreme. Only a full fractional cycle remains, and its local edge equations have the unique solution 1/2 around the cycle exactly for odd parity of side-branch labels; even parity leaves a line. Binary labels propagate uniquely across rooted trees from leaf values. Even leaf parity yields two binary cycle completions, odd parity one half-cycle completion, giving \(2^n\) and \(2^{n-1}\) vertices. Finite graph checks tested n=3 and n=4 with different shapes, but the proof is general. Toric orbit stratification gives \(\chi_{\mathrm{top}}=3\cdot 2^{n-1}\).

broader_coverage.reasoning: The complete Hilbert-function invariance and flat deformation results do not determine an f-vector or fixed-point count: varieties in one flat family may have different Euler characteristics when singular, and polytopes with the same Ehrhart polynomial can have different face numbers. Generator degree bounds do not classify extremal rays/vertices, which are a subset of integral degree-two generators after scaling. An explicit counterexample to a Hilbert-to-face-count implication is the unit square versus the triangle with vertices (0,0), (2,0), (0,1): both have Ehrhart polynomial \( (k+1)^2 \) but respectively four and three vertices.

Proof in RESULT.md classifies every torus-fixed point, not just its number.
value.rationale: The binary symmetric graph model is a natural family at first Betti number one, and torus fixed points are geometric building blocks for localization, orbit structure and singularity investigation. The result is a full structural classification indexed by parity of the actual leaves, not an arbitrary numeric bound. It produces a simple topological Euler characteristic independent of graph shape, a distinct invariant not implied by the published Hilbert-function invariance. The offcycle fractional-support obstruction and odd-cycle parity rigidity are reusable structural arguments.
